title: chore(toolchain): upgrade Flutter 3.41.9 → 3.44.0 (Dart 3.11.5 → 3.12.0) + dependency triage plan
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **⚠️ VERDICT REVISED (2026-05-31) — read the [deep-research correction comment](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/4846#issuecomment-4585804768) first.**
> A follow-up exhaustive audit (deterministic full-lockfile SDK scan + ~80-agent deep web research, adversarially verified) **overturns the "🟢 GREEN / zero source changes" conclusion below.** The bump is feasible but **not zero-touch**: there is a **hard compile blocker** — the `media_kit_video` git fork won't build on 3.44/Dart 3.12 ([media-kit#1418](https://github.com/media-kit/media-kit/issues/1418)) and must be patched first — plus a `ListTile` debug-assert risk and several deprecation hits. The version-**resolvability** analysis in this body still holds (all 353 lock entries resolve); the "no source changes" claim does **not**. Treat the sections below as the resolvability baseline, and the correction comment as the current verdict.

---

## Summary

This issue proposes upgrading our toolchain from **Flutter 3.41.9 / Dart 3.11.5** → **Flutter 3.44.0 / Dart 3.12.0** (latest stable, released 2026-05-18), and lays out a triaged plan for the dependency tree behind it.

The two efforts are **independent and should be decoupled**: the Flutter bump is low-risk and blocks nothing; dependency updates are optional follow-ups done at our own pace.

@hm21 — flagging you for a sanity check before I start. Two specific questions for you near the bottom (build_runner cap + go_router/riverpod majors). Does this sequencing look right to you, and is there anything in our native/media stack you'd want exercised before we cut over?

---

## Baseline (ground truth, verified against the Flutter release index)

| | Version | Dart | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pinned now | Flutter **3.41.9** | Dart **3.11.5** | 2026-04-30 |
| **Target (latest stable)** | Flutter **3.44.0** | Dart **3.12.0** | 2026-05-18 |
| Latest beta (not proposed) | 3.45.0-0.1.pre | 3.13.0 | 2026-05-21 |

This is **one stable cadence step** (Dart 3.11.5 → 3.12.0, a single minor) — not a major jump.

**Local drift to fix while we're here:** bare `flutter` on at least one dev machine resolves to **3.41.1**, while `mobile/mise.toml` pins **3.41.9**. The upgrade is a good moment to realign mise as the single local authority.

---

## Readiness verdict: 🟢 GREEN — low risk

Audit (4 parallel codebase sweeps + direct pub.dev SDK-constraint checks):

1. **Deprecated/removed APIs — ZERO.** Scanned 2,675 Dart files (lib, all packages, test, integration_test, excluding generated). No `WillPopScope`, `RawKeyboard*`, `textScaleFactor`, `.withOpacity`, `MaterialState*`, or integer `Color` getters. Already on `PopScope` / `withValues(alpha:)` / `TextScaler`. **No source changes required for the bump.**
2. **The `build_runner` "blocker" is a false alarm — verified.** Cap is `>=2.7.1 <2.11.0` (TODO #3142, riverpod_generator `InvalidTypeException`), resolved to 2.10.5. Worry was "does Dart 3.12 force build_runner ≥ 2.11?" Answer from pub.dev: **no.** build_runner 2.10.5 declares `sdk: ^3.7.0` (accepts 3.12); analyzer 8.4.0 is `^3.9.0` (accepts 3.12). **The cap stays as-is — no upstream coordination needed.**
3. **Native toolchain — all above Flutter 3.44 minimums:** iOS deploy 16.0, macOS 13.0, Xcode 26.5, Android AGP 8.9.1 / Kotlin 2.1.0 / Gradle 8.12 / NDK 28.2.13676358 / compileSdk 36 / minSdk 28 / Java 17. (Advisory only: Gradle 8.12 is slightly ahead of 3.44's tested band — already works on 3.41, leave it.)
4. **Two git-pinned deps to compile-check** (no SDK-constraint enforcement): `c2pa_flutter @ 0.0.3` and the `media_kit_video` fork commit. Compile under 3.11 today; Dart 3.12 has no language breaking changes, so low risk — the build/test step proves it.

---

## Complete file inventory for the Flutter bump

Verified by a repo-wide scan — **no hidden second source of truth.**

| File | Lines | Change | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mobile/mise.toml` | 2 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | **Local toolchain authority** |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_ci.yaml` | 25, 80, 98, 116 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` (×4 jobs) | CI |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_pr_preview_build.yml` | 37 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | CI |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_service_integration_tests.yaml` | 22 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | CI |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_web_production_deploy.yml` | 34 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | CI |
| `.github/workflows/models_ci.yaml` | 27 | `flutter_version: "3.41.9"` → `"3.44.0"` | CI (reusable input) |
| `.github/workflows/sounds_repository.yaml` | 27 | `flutter_version: "3.41.9"` → `"3.44.0"` | CI (reusable input) |
| `codemagic.yaml` | 371, 431, 477, 530, 561, 598 | `flutter: 3.41.9` → `3.44.0` (×6) | App-store builds |
| `mobile/pubspec.yaml` | 22–23 | floor bump (see note) | constraint |
| ~24 `mobile/packages/*/pubspec.yaml` | — | floor bump (see note) | constraint |
| `mobile/.metadata` | 9 | `channel: "beta"` → `"stable"` | drift cleanup (optional) |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | 145–146 | doc text | docs |
| `mobile/pubspec.lock` | — | **regenerated, not hand-edited** | the real artifact |

**Note on the pubspec floors:** `sdk: ^3.11.0` / `flutter: ^3.41.1` are *floors*, not pins — caret ranges already permit 3.44/Dart 3.12, so resolution works without touching them. Raising to `sdk: ^3.12.0` / `flutter: ^3.44.0` is correct hygiene (a contributor on an old SDK gets a clear error instead of a confusing build failure). If we bump the app floor, bump the package floors for consistency.

---

## The 1.0-confidence procedure (order matters)

Change the toolchain authority first, let tooling regenerate the lockfile, prove it builds/tests, **then** fan the pin out to CI.

```bash
# 0. Branch off origin/main
git fetch origin && git checkout -b chore/flutter-3.44 origin/main

# 1. Bump LOCAL authority first, install, realign drift
#    edit mobile/mise.toml: flutter = "3.44.0"
cd mobile && mise install
mise exec -- flutter --version            # confirm 3.44.0 / Dart 3.12.0

# 2. Regenerate the lockfile under the new SDK (the real change)
mise exec -- flutter pub get
git diff pubspec.lock                      # review (expect minimal)

# 3. Regenerate code (build_runner cap stays — verified compatible)
mise exec -- dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs

# 4. Prove it — the gates that turn "should work" into 1.0
mise exec -- flutter analyze lib test integration_test
mise exec -- flutter test
mise exec -- flutter build apk --debug
mise exec -- flutter build ios --no-codesign
mise exec -- flutter build macos
mise exec -- flutter build web

# 5. Only AFTER local is green: bump the pins everywhere (table above)

# 6. Commit lockfile + generated files + version pins together; push; let CI confirm
```

**Confidence scope:** ~1.0 on the *inventory* (exhaustive, verified) and *static compatibility* (deps, APIs, native toolchain, build_runner cap). The one thing no static analysis can give 1.0 on is "compiles + all tests pass" — that's steps 2–4, which is the final piece of the procedure, not optional.

**Product heads-up for the next cycle (not blocking now):** Flutter 3.44 flags **iOS UIScene lifecycle** and **AGP 9 / KGP** as *future* requirements. Neither breaks us today (AGP 8.9.1 + backward-compat), but worth planning.

---

## Dependency tree (separate, decoupled effort)

Queried pub.dev directly for all ~96 hosted direct deps across the workspace.

**Single most important finding:** **every package's latest version still accepts Dart 3.12 / Flutter 3.44 — zero exceptions.** Nothing in the dependency tree blocks the Flutter upgrade. A plain `flutter pub get` after the bump will **not** pull any of the below — they're held by our `^` constraints, so the upgrade PR stays clean. We opt into these explicitly.

Of 96 hosted direct deps: **42 current, 15 patch-behind, 27 minor-behind, 10 major-behind.**

### 🟢 Tier 1 — safe sweep (patches + low-risk minors), one PR
Pure bugfixes, no API changes:
`dio→5.9.2, freezed→3.2.5, image_picker→1.2.2, permission_handler→12.0.2, shared_preferences→2.5.5, uuid→4.5.3, mocktail→1.0.5, equatable→2.0.8, http→1.6.0, json_serializable→6.14.0, json_annotation→4.12.0, flutter_svg→2.3.0, cupertino_icons→1.0.9, async→2.13.1, webview_flutter→4.13.1, flutter_native_splash→2.4.8, skeletonizer→2.1.3, postgres→3.5.11, connectivity_plus→7.1.1, file_selector→1.1.0` + the **5 Firebase** minors (`firebase_core→4.9.0`, `firebase_analytics→12.4.1`, `firebase_crashlytics→5.2.2`, `firebase_messaging→16.2.2`, `firebase_performance→0.11.4+1` — bump as a co-versioned set). `build_runner→2.15.0` only after confirming #3142's riverpod_generator bug is gone (test codegen).

### 🟡 Tier 2 — major bumps, plugin-only (read changelog, likely mechanical)
Breaking changes usually in native setup, not Dart API. Each its own PR:
`device_info_plus 10→13` (+3 majors, biggest gap), `file_picker 10→11`, `flutter_secure_storage 9→10`, `package_info_plus 9→10`, `share_plus 12→13`, `flutter_web_auth_2 4→5`.

### 🔴 Tier 3 — major bumps needing real code review
- **`go_router 16→17`** — routing is load-bearing (typed routes, redirects, ShellRoute). v17 has API changes; needs careful migration + full nav testing.
- **`riverpod_generator + riverpod_annotation 3→4`** — codegen contract change; regenerate everything + verify; couple with runtime `flutter_riverpod 3.0.3→3.3.1`. This is also where the build_runner #3142 cap lives — untangle first.
- **`google_fonts 6→8`** (+2 majors) — API/asset-loading changes; verify Pacifico / Inter / BricolageGrotesque still resolve.

### 📝 Worth a look
`hive_ce 2.6→2.19` (+13 minors — large drift on our persistence layer; changelog scan), `drift 2.31→2.33` (paired with drift_dev, regen), `patrol 4.2→4.6` (+4, integration-test harness), `sqlite3_flutter_libs→0.6.0+eol` (the `+eol` tag is a flag — check what's deprecated).

---

## Proposed sequencing

1. **Ship the Flutter 3.44 bump alone first** — clean, low-risk, unblocks nothing else.
2. **Then Tier 1** as one "dependency housekeeping" PR — fast, high-confidence.
3. **Then Tier 2/3 individually**, each with its own changelog read + targeted tests. Never batch a major bump with anything else (one-line `git bisect` when something breaks).

---

## Questions for @hm21

1. **build_runner cap (#3142):** I verified the cap doesn't block Dart 3.12, so I'd keep it as-is for the bump. But do you want to bundle an attempt to *lift* it (test whether riverpod_generator 4.x fixes the `InvalidTypeException`) into the riverpod 3→4 PR, or keep that entirely separate?
2. **go_router 16→17 + riverpod 3→4:** these are the two Tier-3 items that touch app/generated code. Any preference on order, or known landmines in our routing/state layers I should plan around?
3. **media stack:** anything in `media_kit` / `media_kit_video` fork / `pro_video_editor` / `pro_image_editor` you'd want explicitly exercised on 3.44 before we cut over (beyond the standard build + test)?
4. **Sequencing:** does "Flutter bump solo → Tier 1 sweep → Tier 2/3 individually" match how you'd want this staged?

> Note: confidence is ~1.0 on the inventory and static compatibility; "compiles + tests pass" and the Tier 2/3 "upgrades without breaking our code" claims are exactly what the per-PR build/test gates establish — not assertable statically.

title: feat(camera): add hold-to-record functionality for video recording
body: Closes #4850 ## Description Discussed on discord [here](https://discord.com/channels/1470168817589158040/1470255950408454164/1510133586047537223) Adds a **hold-to-record** mode to the video recorder, allowing users to start recording by pressing and holding the shutter button and stop by releasing it — in addition to the existing tap-to-record behaviour. **Related Issue:** ### Changes - **`VideoRecorderBloc`** — new `holdToRecord` flag in state; updated start/stop logic to handle press-down / release events - **`VideoRecorderState`** — added `holdToRecord` field - **`HoldToRecordPreferenceService`** — new service backed by `SharedPreferences` to persist the user's preference - **`preferencesProviders`** — exposes the new service via Riverpod - **`GeneralSettingsScreen`** — toggle to enable / disable hold-to-record - **`VideoRecorderClassicStack`** / **`ShutterGestureDetector`** / **`VideoRecorderRecordButton`** — wired up press/release gesture handling - **Localizations** — new `cameraSettingsHoldToRecord` key added to all 20 supported locales and generated files regenerated ## Out of Scope None — follow-up could include hold-to-record support for the web recorder if needed. ## Verification - `flutter analyze` — clean - `flutter test mobile/test/blocs/video_recorder/` — green - `flutter test mobile/test/screens/settings/` — green - `flutter test mobile/test/services/hold_to_record_preference_service_test.dart` — green - `flutter test mobile/test/widgets/video_recorder/` — green - Manually tested tap-to-record and hold-to-record modes on iOS Simulator and Android Emulator ## Type of Change - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

feat: add timeline markers for video and audio sync

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### What would you like?

Add the ability to place markers along the video and audio timeline during editing. Markers could be used to flag important moments like sound effects, impacts, transitions, or cuts so users can quickly align clips and audio without repeatedly scrubbing through the timeline.

### How would this be useful for you?

This would make syncing audio effects much faster and more accurate, especially when fixing missing or desynced audio. Instead of constantly rewinding and retrying adjustments, users could mark key moments and line everything up visually.

### When would you use this?

When editing clips with timed sound effects like Vine Booms, smashes, transitions, or music beats where precise sync matters.

### Anything else?

It could be helpful if markers supported labels or different colors for audio vs video events.

This was requested on discord [here](https://discord.com/channels/1470168817589158040/1470256031434149953/1510445689153388654)
